name: Big Three
description: Big Three (大三, Da San) is a strategic Chinese climbing game for 3 players from the Shaanxi province. It is closely related to games like 'Wa Keng' (Digging the Pit). In each deal, the 3s are the highest-ranking cards, and players bid in an auction to become the 'Declarer' who plays alone against the other two. The game is known for its peculiar ranking (3s high, 2s second) and the restriction that 3s, 2s, and Aces cannot be used in sequences.

overview.description: Big Three (大三, Da San) is a strategic Chinese climbing game for 3 players from the Shaanxi province. It is closely related to games like 'Wa Keng' (Digging the Pit). history.origins: Originating in Shaanxi province, China, as a variation of the broader 'climbing' genre. It specifically targets three-player dynamics, making it a faster and more aggressive alternative to the four-player 'Tractor' family.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Developed as a regional folk game in Northern China.
1990s: Popularized in regional tournaments and under the name 'Wa Keng'.
Present: A staple of Chinese online gaming platforms and social clubs.
history.cultural: Reflects the northern Chinese preference for three-player games, emphasizing individual skill and psychological bidding.
history.evolution: The game shifted from a simple shedding race to an auction-based format where the declarer takes a small widow, adding a tactical 'risk vs reward' phase before play.

setup.dealing: The deck is dealt as follows: 16 cards to each player and 4 cards face down in the center (The Widow).

rules.objective: Be the first to shed all cards from your hand. If the declarer wins, they win points from both opponents; if the opponents win, the declarer pays both.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid 1, 2, or 3 points to take the contract. Highest bidder is Declarer. 2. **Widow**: Declarer takes the 4 cards from the widow into their hand. 3. **Climbing**: Players must play a combination of the same type but higher rank than the previous. 4. **Ranks**: 3 (High) > 2 > A > K > Q ... > 4 (Low). 5. **Combinations**: Singles, Pairs, Triples, and Sequences.
keyRules: 3s, 2s, and Aces cannot be part of a sequence (e.g., Q-K-A is illegal).
A Triple of 3s is an invincible 'Bomb' in some variations.
Players can pass on any turn, even if they can beat the current combo.

strategy.basic: Don't overbid for the Declarer role unless you hold at least one 3 and several 2s. The widow is small and rarely fixes a terrible hand.
strategy.intermediate: Counting the 3s: There are only four 3s in the deck. If you hold three of them, you control the game. Force opponents to waste their 3s on single cards.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Lead: As an opponent, lead a combo type the Declarer is likely weak in. If they passed on a pair earlier, keep leading pairs to prevent them from shedding their singles.
tips: Save your 3s to regain the lead when you have a long sequence to dump.
If you are an opponent, communicate through your plays—don't trap your partner!

variations.name: Wa Keng (Digging the Pit)
variations.description: Essentially the same game, but with different scoring multipliers for specific 'bombs'.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No separate engine configuration is needed; Wa Keng uses the same structure and only tweaks scoring multipliers outside the core blueprint.

scoring.description: Points are awarded based on the bid level. Declarer wins bid amount from each opponent (x2) or loses it to each.
scoring.winCondition: Highest point total after a set session or reaching a target score.

synthesis.shortDescription: A fierce three-player climbing game from Northern China. Bid for the privilege of taking the 'Widow' and playing solo against your rivals. With 3s at the top of the hierarchy and strict sequence rules, Big Three is a masterclass in hand management and tactical passing.
